title: document-engineering ships three component tiers: /scalars needs a Form wrapper, /ui does not, and /table holds ObjectSetTable
content:
`@powerhousedao/document-engineering` exposes several entry points, and picking the wrong one is a common early stumble because the components have overlapping names.

**`/scalars`** holds the form tier. Each component corresponds to a GraphQL scalar type — `StringField`, `BooleanField`, `NumberField`, `PHIDField`, `AmountField`, `CurrencyCodeField` (note: there is **no** `CurrencyField` — that identifier has zero hits in the repo; the real components are `currency-code-field` and `amount-field`) — and they are built on react-hook-form. They ship out-of-the-box validation, and the price is that **they must be wrapped in the `Form` component from the same package** or they will not work properly. Even a single checkbox needs the wrapper:

```tsx
import { Form, BooleanField } from "@powerhousedao/document-engineering/scalars";

export const Checkbox = ({ value, onChange }: CheckboxProps) => (
  <Form onSubmit={() => {}}>
    <BooleanField name="checked" description="Mark as complete" value={value} onChange={onChange} />
  </Form>
);
```

Note the `onSubmit={() => {}}` — in a Powerhouse editor there is no form submission, because changes go out as dispatched actions on change. The `Form` is there purely to provide the react-hook-form context.

**`/ui`** holds the general-purpose tier: simplified variants of the scalar components that need no `Form` wrapper but correspondingly lack the built-in validation, plus components with no scalar counterpart at all — `Dropdown`, `Tooltip`, `Sidebar`, `Button`, `Icon` and more (`src/ui/components/`). This is where you go for layout and interaction rather than data entry.

**`/table`** is its own tier, and this is where `ObjectSetTable` actually lives (`src/table/index.ts` re-exports it from `./table/object-set-table.js`) — **not** under `/ui`, as is easy to assume.

The complete export surface in `package.json` is: `.`, `./scalars`, `./scalars/*`, `./ui`, `./ui/*`, `./table`, `./table/*`, `./graphql`, `./graphql/*`, `./graphql-scalars`, `./graphql-scalars/*`, and `./style.css`. `./graphql` maps to `src/scalars/graphql/`, the scalar definitions themselves. Inside the repo the same surfaces are reachable via import maps `#assets`, `#scalars`, `#ui` and `#graphql`.

The practical rule: reach for `/scalars` when the component *is* a document-model field and you want validation for free; reach for `/ui` when you are composing an interface. And treat the component's source as the final word on props — Storybook documents common props but may lag or omit some.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/05-EditorsUI/00-DocumentEngineering.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._

_Source-verified 2026-08-13 against the document-engineering repo at v1.40.5 (`/home/p/Powerhouse/document-engineering`), a separate repo from the powerhouse monorepo._
description: /scalars is react-hook-form based and must be wrapped in Form. /ui is validation-free layout components. ObjectSetTable lives in /table, not /ui. There is no CurrencyField.
